reference: No GNU uuencode executable is installed in the host reference PATH. Contract outputs were generated independently: Python 3 binascii.b2a_uu(..., backtick=True) for classic uu lines, RFC 4648 base64 via Python base64.b64encode for -m lines, with independently specified 45-byte chunks and format headers/trailers. Metadata help expectation uses Bash help formatting: the registered usage string followed by each public documentation string; type output uses Bash builtin metadata.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
classic uu encoding of binary and empty stdin
named-file and stdin permission headers under a nondefault umask
explicit '-' stdin operand and repeated stdin redirections in one Bash process
exclusions: GNU byte-for-byte parity is unavailable because no uuencode CLI is installed; all runnable cases are explicitly contract cases, not claimed GNU parity.
No deferred operation case is needed: this encoder uses ordinary fixture data and does not require privilege, hardware, a terminal driver, or a network peer.

cases.purpose: Bash reports the registered loadable as a builtin; metadata only, not operation coverage.
The Bash help text matches the loadable's documented command summary and synopsis.
cases.stdout:
uuencode: uuencode [-m] [FILE] NAME
    Encode FILE or stdin in uuencode format (classic uu, or base64 with -m).
        uuencode [-m] [FILE] NAME

cases.purpose: Classic uu encoding preserves NUL, control, high-bit, and ordinary bytes in one short stdin payload.
An empty classic input still emits the length-zero terminator and end marker.
A 46-byte classic input produces a full 45-byte line followed by a one-byte line.
cases.script: for ((i=0; i<46; i++)); do printf '%d' "$((i % 10))"; done | uuencode wrap.dat

cases.purpose: The -m mode uses RFC 4648 base64 padding for a two-byte input and emits its format trailer.
The -m mode wraps after 45 input bytes and puts the final byte in a padded second line.
cases.script: for ((i=0; i<46; i++)); do printf '%d' "$((i % 10))"; done | uuencode -m wrapped.dat

cases.purpose: A named input reports its created 0640 mode; stdin uses 0666 masked by umask 027 in classic and base64 headers.
cases.script: umask 027; printf 'source-content\n' > input.dat; uuencode input.dat 'remote/path with spaces'; printf 'stdin-content\n' | uuencode -m base64-name
cases.stdout:
begin 640 remote/path with spaces
/<V]U<F-E+6-O;G1E;G0*
`
end
begin-base64 640 base64-name
c3RkaW4tY29udGVudAo=
====

cases.purpose: An explicit FILE operand of - reads stdin and uses the default masked stdin mode.
Two stdin redirections in one Bash process encode both distinct files, guarding against a stale EOF indicator.
cases.script: printf 'first\n' > first.dat; printf 'second\n' > second.dat; uuencode first.out < first.dat; uuencode second.out < second.dat
cases.stdout:
begin 644 first.out
&9FER<W0*
`
end
begin 644 second.out
'<V5C;VYD"@``
`
end

cases.purpose: The documented synopsis requires a decode name; omitting all operands reports usage and exits with EX_USAGE.
A missing named source fails before producing an encoded header and emits a diagnostic.
Empty RFC 4648 payload emits framing and trailer only.
